script.title: How Digging a Well Uncovered an Underground Army
script.hook_text: Farmers dug into an underground army
sentences: In 1974, farmers digging a well struck an underground army.
Yang Zhifa and his family were simply looking for water outside Xi'an.
Their shovels hit baked clay seven meters beneath the soil.
Chinese archaeologists arrived to investigate the damaged pottery fragments.
Instead of a small find, the trenches opened into massive underground corridors.
Each life-sized figure had an individual face, uniform, and rank.
They had uncovered over eight thousand clay soldiers, buried to guard China's first emperor in the afterlife.
All of it remained hidden until someone needed water.
script.description:
In 1974, local farmers outside Xi'an set out to dig a water well.
They ended up uncovering the eight-thousand-strong Terracotta Army.
visuals: Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor mound
claims_en: Farmers digging a well discovered the Terracotta Army in 1974 outside Xi'an.
The discovery group included Yang Zhifa and his brothers searching for water.
The pits containing the army were found seven meters deep.
Chinese archaeologists arrived to investigate the terracotta fragments.
Excavation trenches revealed massive underground corridors containing figures.
The terracotta soldiers are life-sized and each figure features individual facial features and uniforms according to rank.
The pits hold more than 8,000 soldiers buried to protect China's first emperor Qin Shi Huang in the afterlife.
